summary: Mission Peak lookout built 1934 near Wenatchee, removed around 1945; a 2019 trip report says it is long gone and the old lookout road is now a trail.

facts.design: 10 ft pole L-4 tower per three histories; a 1934 newspaper describes a 15 ft tower
facts.status_note: Removed, possibly around 1945; a 2019 trip report says the lookout is long gone.

visit.trail_note: About 2 miles and 1,000 feet of gain on Rd 330, now a trail, starting from Liberty-Beehive Rd 9712.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Firetower.org, firelookout.com and WillhiteWeb describe a 10 ft pole L-4 tower; the 1934 Wenatchee Daily World story, as reprinted on the Forest Lookouts page, describes a 15 ft tower. The record's 4.6 m matches 15 ft. The story reports both and does not choose.

The 1933 name is spelled Guilberson on the Forest Lookouts page and Guiberson on firelookout.com. A climbing-page photo caption names Hank Kuch where the 1934 newspapers name Oscar Kuntz. The story uses the newspaper spellings and says the caption name could not be matched.

Firetower.org and firelookout.com both say it was removed at some point and may not have lasted much longer than 1945; WillhiteWeb says possibly around 1945; firelookout.com lists the site as 1934-?. No source gives a firm removal date, and the story says so.

notes_for_editor: Brief height_m 4.6 equals the 15 ft figure from the 1934 newspaper; three lookout histories say 10 ft (about 3.0 m). The record was not changed, so the editor can choose. Staffing names are unresolved (Guilberson or Guiberson; Kuntz or Kuch). The only description of the site today is a 2019 trip report, which is the basis for the access route. The Wikipedia article was checked and mentions no lookout.
